defmodule ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.Worker do
  @moduledoc """
  The OCR -> extraction -> verification pipeline for a single document.

  `run/1` executes one attempt and returns `{:ok, content} | {:error, reason}`.
  It persists a SUCCESS row itself but never persists a failure: the durable
  `ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.OCRJob` decides whether and when to record a
  failure based on `ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ErrorClassification` and the
  attempt number, so retries never multiply failed rows.

  Every terminal write (success and failure rows) is serialized per document:
  inside its transaction it locks the document row and re-checks the latest
  extraction against the expected id from enqueue time, so overlapping
  executions cannot append two terminal rows. A changed document rolls back
  with `:already_processed`; a deleted one with `:document_deleted`.

  The TypeSafe shadow enqueue is fail-open: a changeset-level enqueue failure
  commits the extraction with an `enqueue_failed` shadow (the job insert is
  savepoint-isolated inside the success transaction), while a raised DB
  exception still rolls back the whole terminal write and surfaces to the
  durable `OCRJob` for retry.
  """

  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.DocumentOCR
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContentContext
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.TemporaryFile
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Document
  alias ZaimuTomo.Langfuse
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review
  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage
  import Ecto.Query, only: [from: 2]
  require Logger

  @doc """
  Runs one processing attempt for a self-contained command:

      %{document: %Document{}, currency_hint: String.t(), supersedes_extraction_id: id | nil}

  Returns `{:ok, %ExtractedContent{}}` when a success row was persisted,
  `{:error, :already_processed | :document_deleted}` when the terminal write
  was superseded or the document is gone, or `{:error, reason}` without
  persisting anything so the caller can retry or record a single failure.
  """
  def run(%{
        document: %{object_key: object_key} = document,
        currency_hint: currency_hint,
        supersedes_extraction_id: expected_extraction_id
      }) do
    Langfuse.trace_document_processing(document, fn ->
      trace_id = Langfuse.current_trace_id()

      case TemporaryFile.create(object_key) do
        {:ok, temporary_path} ->
          try do
            with {:ok, ^temporary_path} <- Storage.get_object(object_key, temporary_path),
                 {:ok, markdown, raw_llm_response} <- DocumentOCR.process(temporary_path),
                 {:ok, extracted_data} <-
                   ZaimuTomo.LLMClient.extract_invoice(markdown, currency_hint),
                 {:ok, verification} <-
                   ZaimuTomo.LLMClient.verify_extraction(markdown, extracted_data) do
              persist_and_emit_success(
                document,
                extracted_data,
                raw_llm_response,
                verification,
                trace_id,
                currency_hint,
                expected_extraction_id
              )
            end
          after
            File.rm(temporary_path)
          end

        {:error, posix} ->
          {:error, {:scratch_unavailable, posix}}
      end
    end)
  end

  def persist_and_emit_success(
        document,
        extracted_data,
        raw_llm_response,
        verification,
        trace_id,
        currency_hint,
        expected_extraction_id \\ nil
      ) do
    analysis = %{
      "processed_at" => DateTime.utc_now(),
      "verification" => verification
    }

    extraction_params = %{
      document_id: document.id,
      user_id: document.user_id,
      extracted_data: extracted_data,
      raw_llm_response: raw_llm_response,
      analysis: analysis,
      status: "success",
      trace_id: trace_id
    }

    Repo.transaction(fn ->
      lock_and_check_latest(document.id, expected_extraction_id)

      with {:ok, content} <- ExtractedContentContext.create_extracted_content(extraction_params),
           {:ok, _review_decision} <- Review.create_initial_decision(content) do
        # The TypeSafe shadow job is inserted in this transaction so a shadow
        # run cannot be lost between commit and enqueue.
        enqueue_typesafe_shadow(content, currency_hint)
        content
      else
        {:error, changeset} -> Repo.rollback({:persistence_failed, changeset.errors})
      end
    end)
    |> case do
      {:ok, content} ->
        DocumentProcessing.broadcast_event(:success, document.user_id, %{
          document_id: document.id,
          extraction_id: content.id,
          user_id: document.user_id,
          status: :completed,
          data: extracted_data,
          timestamp: DateTime.utc_now()
        })

        {:ok, content}

      {:error, :already_processed} ->
        {:error, :already_processed}

      {:error, :document_deleted} ->
        {:error, :document_deleted}

      {:error, {:persistence_failed, errors}} ->
        Logger.error(
          "[OCR] Failed to persist successful extraction for document #{document.id}: #{inspect(errors)}"
        )

        {:error, {:persistence_failed, errors}}
    end
  end

  def persist_and_emit_failure(document, error, expected_extraction_id \\ nil) do
    error_details = %{
      "type" => error_type(error),
      "message" => error_message(error),
      "stack_trace" => error_stack_trace(error),
      "timestamp" => DateTime.utc_now()
    }

    # Failed extractions persist an empty extracted-data embed because invoice
    # fields are unavailable when processing does not complete.
    extraction_params = %{
      document_id: document.id,
      user_id: document.user_id,
      # Empty map - will fail validation as expected
      extracted_data: %{},
      analysis: %{
        "error" => "Extraction failed",
        "attempted_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
      },
      status: "failed",
      error_details: error_details
    }

    Repo.transaction(fn ->
      lock_and_check_latest(document.id, expected_extraction_id)

      with {:ok, content} <- ExtractedContentContext.create_extracted_content(extraction_params),
           {:ok, _review_decision} <- Review.create_failed_decision(content, error) do
        content
      else
        {:error, changeset} -> Repo.rollback({:persistence_failed, changeset.errors})
      end
    end)
    |> case do
      {:ok, content} ->
        DocumentProcessing.broadcast_event(:failed, document.user_id, %{
          document_id: document.id,
          extraction_id: content.id,
          user_id: document.user_id,
          status: :failed,
          error: error,
          timestamp: DateTime.utc_now()
        })

        {:ok, content}

      {:error, :already_processed} ->
        {:error, :already_processed}

      {:error, :document_deleted} ->
        {:error, :document_deleted}

      {:error, {:persistence_failed, errors}} ->
        Logger.error(
          "[OCR] Failed to persist failed extraction for document #{document.id}: #{inspect(errors)}"
        )

        {:error, {:persistence_failed, errors}}
    end
  end

  # Serialize one document's terminal write: lock the document row, then
  # re-check the latest extraction against the expected id from enqueue time.
  # An overlapping run that already appended a row rolls the transaction back
  # with :already_processed; a deleted document with :document_deleted.
  defp lock_and_check_latest(document_id, expected_extraction_id) do
    case Repo.one(from(d in Document, where: d.id == ^document_id, lock: "FOR UPDATE")) do
      nil ->
        Repo.rollback(:document_deleted)

      %Document{} ->
        case ExtractedContentContext.get_latest_by_document(document_id) do
          nil when is_nil(expected_extraction_id) -> :ok
          %{id: ^expected_extraction_id} -> :ok
          _newer -> Repo.rollback(:already_processed)
        end
    end
  end

  # TypeSafe shadow runs are best-effort: a failed enqueue is recorded on the
  # row but never rolls back the invoice extraction. The currency hint is a
  # required argument — a missing hint is a caller bug, never a silent skip.
  #
  # Only ever called from inside the success transaction (the SAVEPOINT below
  # requires an open transaction; there is no fallback path). The job insert is
  # isolated with raw-SQL savepoints because Oban drops :mode from insert
  # options and Ecto nested transactions are not savepoints. Only a changeset
  # error is contained here: a raised exception rolls back the whole terminal
  # write and surfaces to the durable OCRJob for retry.
  defp enqueue_typesafe_shadow(content, currency_hint) when is_binary(currency_hint) do
    if ZaimuTomo.TypeSafeClient.enabled?() do
      Repo.query!("SAVEPOINT typesafe_enqueue")

      case ZaimuTomo.TypeSafeVerification.enqueue(%{
             extracted_content_id: content.id,
             currency_hint: currency_hint
           }) do
        {:ok, _job} ->
          Repo.query!("RELEASE SAVEPOINT typesafe_enqueue")
          :ok

        {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} ->
          Repo.query!("ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT typesafe_enqueue")

          Logger.warning("[TypeSafe] Shadow verification enqueue failed class=enqueue_failed",
            typesafe_error_class: "enqueue_failed"
          )

          _result =
            ExtractedContentContext.put_typesafe_shadow(content.id, %{
              "status" => "verification_failed",
              "error" => "enqueue_failed"
            })

          :ok
      end
    else
      Logger.debug("[TypeSafe] Shadow verification skipped")
    end
  end

  # Error handling helper functions
  defp error_type(error) when is_tuple(error),
    do: elem(error, 0) |> to_string()

  defp error_type(error) when is_atom(error),
    do: Atom.to_string(error)

  defp error_type(_error),
    do: "unknown"

  defp error_message({_tag, %{reason: reason}}) when is_binary(reason), do: reason

  defp error_message(error) when is_tuple(error) do
    val = elem(error, 1)
    if is_binary(val), do: val, else: inspect(val)
  end

  defp error_message(error) when is_atom(error), do: Atom.to_string(error)
  defp error_message(error) when is_binary(error), do: error
  defp error_message(error), do: inspect(error)

  defp error_stack_trace(_error),
    do: []
end

1	defmodule ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  The DocumentProcessing context.
4	
5	  Builds durable OCR job commands that Oban dispatches. The enqueue is atomic
6	  with the document insert (see `ZaimuTomo.Documents.create_document/2`), so an
7	  upload can never exist without its processing job.
8	
9	  Also owns the processing state of a document and the scope-checked retry
10	  entry point for failed or stuck runs.
11	  """
12	
13	  import Ecto.Query
14	
15	  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounts.Scope
16	  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
17	  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContentContext
18	  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.OCRJob
19	  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Document
20	  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo
21	
22	  @ocr_job_worker "ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.OCRJob"
23	  @live_job_states ~w(available scheduled executing retryable)
24	  @event_kinds [:success, :failed, :retried]
25	
26	  @typedoc """
27	  Processing state of a document:
28	
29	    * `:processing` — a live OCR job exists (queued, scheduled or running)
30	    * `:stuck` — no extraction and no live job (the run was lost)
31	    * `:failed` — the latest extraction failed
32	    * `:extracted` — the latest extraction succeeded
33	  """
34	  @type processing_state :: :processing | :stuck | :failed | :extracted
35	
36	  @doc """
37	  Subscribes the caller to the scope owner's processing events.
38	
39	  Messages are the maps broadcast by `broadcast_event/3`: a run finished
40	  (`:success` / `:failed`) or a retry was enqueued (`:retried`). Topics are per
41	  owner, so a subscriber never receives another user's extracted data.
42	  """
43	  @spec subscribe_events(Scope.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
44	  def subscribe_events(%Scope{user: %{id: user_id}}) do
45	    Enum.find_value(@event_kinds, :ok, fn kind ->
46	      case Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(ZaimuTomo.PubSub, event_topic(user_id, kind)) do
47	        :ok -> nil
48	        error -> error
49	      end
50	    end)
51	  end
52	
53	  @doc false
54	  @spec broadcast_event(:success | :failed | :retried, integer(), map()) ::
55	          :ok | {:error, term()}
56	  def broadcast_event(kind, user_id, payload) when kind in @event_kinds do
57	    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(ZaimuTomo.PubSub, event_topic(user_id, kind), payload)
58	  end
59	
60	  defp event_topic(user_id, kind), do: "user:#{user_id}:document_processing:#{kind}"
61	
62	  @doc """
63	  Builds the OCR job changeset for a document.
64	
65	  The command is self-contained and resolved at enqueue time: the document id,
66	  a queue-time snapshot of the owner's base currency (`currency_hint`), and the
67	  latest extraction id to supersede (or `nil` when there is none). The worker
68	  pattern-matches this command and never queries Accounts.
69	  """

defmodule ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing do
  @moduledoc """
  The DocumentProcessing context.

  Builds durable OCR job commands that Oban dispatches. The enqueue is atomic
  with the document insert (see `ZaimuTomo.Documents.create_document/2`), so an
  upload can never exist without its processing job.

  Also owns the processing state of a document and the scope-checked retry
  entry point for failed or stuck runs.
  """

  import Ecto.Query

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounts.Scope
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContentContext
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.OCRJob
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Document
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo

  @ocr_job_worker "ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.OCRJob"
  @live_job_states ~w(available scheduled executing retryable)
  @event_kinds [:success, :failed, :retried]

  @typedoc """
  Processing state of a document:

    * `:processing` — a live OCR job exists (queued, scheduled or running)
    * `:stuck` — no extraction and no live job (the run was lost)
    * `:failed` — the latest extraction failed
    * `:extracted` — the latest extraction succeeded
  """
  @type processing_state :: :processing | :stuck | :failed | :extracted

  @doc """
  Subscribes the caller to the scope owner's processing events.

  Messages are the maps broadcast by `broadcast_event/3`: a run finished
  (`:success` / `:failed`) or a retry was enqueued (`:retried`). Topics are per
  owner, so a subscriber never receives another user's extracted data.
  """
  @spec subscribe_events(Scope.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
  def subscribe_events(%Scope{user: %{id: user_id}}) do
    Enum.find_value(@event_kinds, :ok, fn kind ->
      case Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(ZaimuTomo.PubSub, event_topic(user_id, kind)) do
        :ok -> nil
        error -> error
      end
    end)
  end

  @doc false
  @spec broadcast_event(:success | :failed | :retried, integer(), map()) ::
          :ok | {:error, term()}
  def broadcast_event(kind, user_id, payload) when kind in @event_kinds do
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(ZaimuTomo.PubSub, event_topic(user_id, kind), payload)
  end

  defp event_topic(user_id, kind), do: "user:#{user_id}:document_processing:#{kind}"

  @doc """
  Builds the OCR job changeset for a document.

  The command is self-contained and resolved at enqueue time: the document id,
  a queue-time snapshot of the owner's base currency (`currency_hint`), and the
  latest extraction id to supersede (or `nil` when there is none). The worker
  pattern-matches this command and never queries Accounts.
  """
  def ocr_job(%Document{} = document, currency_hint, supersedes_extraction_id) do
    OCRJob.new(%{
      document_id: document.id,
      currency_hint: currency_hint,
      supersedes_extraction_id: supersedes_extraction_id
    })
  end

  @doc """
  Returns the processing state of a document.
  """
  @spec processing_state(Document.t()) :: processing_state()
  def processing_state(%Document{} = document) do
    latest = ExtractedContentContext.get_latest_by_document(document.id)
    classify_state(live_job?(document.id), latest)
  end

  @doc """
  Returns the processing state of many documents at once.

  Same semantics as `processing_state/1`, but resolved with two queries
  (live jobs and latest extraction per document) regardless of how many ids are
  given. Use it wherever a list of documents needs their current state.
  """
  @spec processing_states([pos_integer()]) :: %{pos_integer() => processing_state()}
  def processing_states([]), do: %{}

  def processing_states(document_ids) when is_list(document_ids) do
    live_ids =
      live_jobs()
      |> where(
        [j],
        fragment("?->>'document_id'", j.args) in ^Enum.map(document_ids, &to_string/1)
      )
      |> select([j], fragment("?->>'document_id'", j.args))
      |> Repo.all()
      |> MapSet.new()

    latest_statuses =
      ExtractedContent
      |> where([ec], ec.document_id in ^document_ids)
      |> distinct([ec], ec.document_id)
      |> order_by([ec], asc: ec.document_id, desc: ec.inserted_at, desc: ec.id)
      |> select([ec], {ec.document_id, ec.status})
      |> Repo.all()
      |> Map.new()

    Map.new(document_ids, fn id ->
      latest = latest_statuses[id] && %{status: latest_statuses[id]}
      {id, classify_state(MapSet.member?(live_ids, to_string(id)), latest)}
    end)
  end

  defp classify_state(true, _latest), do: :processing
  defp classify_state(false, nil), do: :stuck
  defp classify_state(false, %{status: "failed"}), do: :failed
  defp classify_state(false, %{status: "success"}), do: :extracted

  @doc """
  Retries processing for a document whose latest run failed or stalled.

  The document must be a persisted struct obtained through a scoped getter
  (e.g. `ZaimuTomo.Documents.get_document!/2`), matching the trust model of
  `ZaimuTomo.Documents.update_document/3`.
  Scope-checked: a document owned by another user returns `{:error, :not_found}`.
  Only `:failed` and `:stuck` are retryable; any other state returns
  `{:error, {:not_retryable, state}}`. The enqueue carries the latest extraction
  id as `supersedes_extraction_id` (nil when stuck), and failed rows are kept as
  history — the new run appends a row. An Oban uniqueness conflict counts as
  success: at most one live job can exist per document.
  """
  @spec retry_document(Scope.t(), Document.t()) ::
          {:ok, Oban.Job.t()} | {:error, :not_found | {:not_retryable, processing_state()}}
  def retry_document(%Scope{user: %{id: user_id}} = scope, %Document{user_id: user_id} = document) do
    latest = ExtractedContentContext.get_latest_by_document(document.id)

    case classify_state(live_job?(document.id), latest) do
      state when state in [:failed, :stuck] ->
        with {:ok, job} <-
               document
               |> ocr_job(scope.user.base_currency, latest && latest.id)
               |> Oban.insert() do
          # Lets open Index / hero views pick up the new live run without a reload.
          broadcast_event(:retried, user_id, %{document_id: document.id, user_id: user_id})
          {:ok, job}
        end

      state ->
        {:error, {:not_retryable, state}}
    end
  end

  def retry_document(%Scope{}, %Document{}), do: {:error, :not_found}

  @doc """
  Returns true when a live OCR job exists for the document.
  """
  @spec live_job?(pos_integer()) :: boolean()
  def live_job?(document_id) do
    # Same safe text comparison as Recovery.list_stuck/0: no ::bigint cast on
    # job args, so a malformed job (missing or non-numeric document_id) is
    # simply not a match and never raises.
    live_jobs()
    |> where([j], fragment("?->>'document_id' = ?", j.args, ^to_string(document_id)))
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
    |> case do
      %Oban.Job{} -> true
      nil -> false
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Base query over live OCR jobs (worker + states that still count as in-flight).
  """
  @spec live_jobs() :: Ecto.Query.t()
  def live_jobs do
    from j in Oban.Job,
      where: j.worker == @ocr_job_worker,
      where: j.state in @live_job_states
  end
end

  @moduledoc """
  Unscoped maintenance recovery for stuck documents: no extraction row and no

  Grouped per user so each run uses the owner's own base currency snapshot,

  """

  import Ecto.Query

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounts.User
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Document
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo

  @type group :: %{user_id: pos_integer(), currency: String.t(), document_ids: [pos_integer()]}

  @doc """

  with that user's base currency.

  Intentionally unscoped: maintenance commands operate on the complete document
  collection (like `ZaimuTomo.Documents.list_document_object_keys/0`).

    # (missing or non-numeric document_id) neither hides every document (as a
    # NULL-poisoned NOT IN would) nor raises (as a ::bigint cast would).

      as: :doc,
      join: u in User,
      on: u.id == d.user_id,
      left_join: ec in ExtractedContent,
      on: ec.document_id == d.id,
      where: is_nil(ec.id),
      where:
        not exists(
          from(j in DocumentProcessing.live_jobs(),
            where: fragment("?->>'document_id' = ?::text", j.args, parent_as(:doc).id),
            select: 1

1	defmodule ZaimuTomo.Documents do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  The Documents context.
4	  """
5	
6	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
7	
8	  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounts.Scope
9	  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing
10	  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
11	  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Document
12	  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Fingerprint
13	  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo
14	  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage
15	
16	  @doc """
17	  Returns a portable object key for an uploaded file.
18	  """
19	  def object_key_for(filename) when is_binary(filename) do
20	    "documents/#{Ecto.UUID.generate()}#{Path.extname(filename)}"
21	  end
22	
23	  @doc """
24	  Reads an uploaded file, stores its bytes, and fingerprints them.
25	
26	  The SHA-256 is computed over the exact binary passed to
27	  `Storage.put_object/2`, so the returned key and digest always describe the
28	  same bytes. Returns attributes ready for `create_document/2` or
29	  `update_document/3`; the caller owns deleting the object if persisting the
30	  row fails.
31	
32	  ## Examples
33	
34	      iex> store_upload("/tmp/plug-123", "invoice.pdf")
35	      {:ok, %{object_key: "documents/….pdf", filename: "invoice.pdf", content_sha256: "…"}}
36	
37	  """
38	  @spec store_upload(Path.t(), String.t()) ::
39	          {:ok, %{object_key: String.t(), filename: String.t(), content_sha256: String.t()}}
40	          | {:error, term()}
41	  def store_upload(path, filename) when is_binary(path) and is_binary(filename) do
42	    object_key = object_key_for(filename)
43	
44	    with {:ok, body} <- File.read(path),
45	         content_sha256 = Fingerprint.sha256(body),
46	         {:ok, ^object_key} <- Storage.put_object(object_key, body) do
47	      {:ok, %{object_key: object_key, filename: filename, content_sha256: content_sha256}}
48	    else
49	      {:ok, _other_key} -> {:error, :unexpected_object_key}
50	      {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}
51	    end
52	  end
53	
54	  @doc """
55	  Subscribes to scoped notifications about any document changes.
56	
57	  The broadcasted messages match the pattern:
58	
59	    * {:created, %Document{}}
60	    * {:updated, %Document{}}
61	    * {:deleted, %Document{}}
62	
63	  """
64	  def subscribe_documents(%Scope{} = scope) do
65	    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(ZaimuTomo.PubSub, documents_topic(scope))
66	  end
67	
68	  defp broadcast_document(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
69	    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(ZaimuTomo.PubSub, documents_topic(scope), message)
70	  end
71	
72	  defp documents_topic(%Scope{} = scope), do: "user:#{scope.user.id}:documents"
73	
74	  @doc """
75	  Returns the list of documents.
76	
77	  ## Examples
78	
79	      iex> list_documents(scope)
80	      [%Document{}, ...]
81	
82	  """
83	  def list_documents(%Scope{} = scope) do
84	    ec_query =
85	      from ec in ExtractedContent,
86	        order_by: [desc: ec.inserted_at, desc: ec.id],
87	        preload: [review_decision: :journal_entry]
88	
89	    from(d in Document,
90	      where: d.user_id == ^scope.user.id,
91	      order_by: [desc: d.inserted_at],
92	      preload: [extracted_content: ^ec_query]
93	    )
94	    |> Repo.all()
95	  end
96	
97	  @doc """
98	  Returns every persisted document object key in a stable order.
99	
100	  This is intentionally unscoped because storage maintenance commands verify
101	  the complete document collection.
102	  """
103	  def list_document_object_keys do
104	    from(d in Document,
105	      order_by: [asc: d.id],
106	      select: d.object_key
107	    )
108	    |> Repo.all()
109	  end
110	
111	  @doc """
112	  Gets a single document.
113	
114	  Raises `Ecto.NoResultsError` if the Document does not exist.
115	
116	  ## Examples
117	
118	      iex> get_document!(scope, 123)
119	      %Document{}
120	
121	      iex> get_document!(scope, 456)
122	      ** (Ecto.NoResultsError)
123	
124	  """
125	  def get_document!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
126	    Repo.get_by!(Document, id: id, user_id: scope.user.id)
127	  end
128	
129	  @doc """
130	  Fetches a document within the authenticated scope.
131	
132	  Returns `{:error, :not_found}` when the document does not exist or belongs to
133	  another user, so callers can treat inaccessible documents as missing.
134	
135	  ## Examples
136	
137	      iex> fetch_document(scope, "123")
138	      {:ok, %Document{}}
139	
140	      iex> fetch_document(scope, "999")
141	      {:error, :not_found}
142	
143	  """

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Documents do
  @moduledoc """
  The Documents context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounts.Scope
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Document
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Fingerprint
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo
  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage

  @doc """
  Returns a portable object key for an uploaded file.
  """
  def object_key_for(filename) when is_binary(filename) do
    "documents/#{Ecto.UUID.generate()}#{Path.extname(filename)}"
  end

  @doc """
  Reads an uploaded file, stores its bytes, and fingerprints them.

  The SHA-256 is computed over the exact binary passed to
  `Storage.put_object/2`, so the returned key and digest always describe the
  same bytes. Returns attributes ready for `create_document/2` or
  `update_document/3`; the caller owns deleting the object if persisting the
  row fails.

  ## Examples

      iex> store_upload("/tmp/plug-123", "invoice.pdf")
      {:ok, %{object_key: "documents/….pdf", filename: "invoice.pdf", content_sha256: "…"}}

  """
  @spec store_upload(Path.t(), String.t()) ::
          {:ok, %{object_key: String.t(), filename: String.t(), content_sha256: String.t()}}
          | {:error, term()}
  def store_upload(path, filename) when is_binary(path) and is_binary(filename) do
    object_key = object_key_for(filename)

    with {:ok, body} <- File.read(path),
         content_sha256 = Fingerprint.sha256(body),
         {:ok, ^object_key} <- Storage.put_object(object_key, body) do
      {:ok, %{object_key: object_key, filename: filename, content_sha256: content_sha256}}
    else
      {:ok, _other_key} -> {:error, :unexpected_object_key}
      {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Subscribes to scoped notifications about any document changes.

  The broadcasted messages match the pattern:

    * {:created, %Document{}}
    * {:updated, %Document{}}
    * {:deleted, %Document{}}

  """
  def subscribe_documents(%Scope{} = scope) do
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(ZaimuTomo.PubSub, documents_topic(scope))
  end

  defp broadcast_document(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(ZaimuTomo.PubSub, documents_topic(scope), message)
  end

  defp documents_topic(%Scope{} = scope), do: "user:#{scope.user.id}:documents"

  @doc """
  Returns the list of documents.

  ## Examples

      iex> list_documents(scope)
      [%Document{}, ...]

  """
  def list_documents(%Scope{} = scope) do
    ec_query =
      from ec in ExtractedContent,
        order_by: [desc: ec.inserted_at, desc: ec.id],
        preload: [review_decision: :journal_entry]

    from(d in Document,
      where: d.user_id == ^scope.user.id,
      order_by: [desc: d.inserted_at],
      preload: [extracted_content: ^ec_query]
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Returns every persisted document object key in a stable order.

  This is intentionally unscoped because storage maintenance commands verify
  the complete document collection.
  """
  def list_document_object_keys do
    from(d in Document,
      order_by: [asc: d.id],
      select: d.object_key
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Gets a single document.

  Raises `Ecto.NoResultsError` if the Document does not exist.

  ## Examples

      iex> get_document!(scope, 123)
      %Document{}

      iex> get_document!(scope, 456)
      ** (Ecto.NoResultsError)

  """
  def get_document!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    Repo.get_by!(Document, id: id, user_id: scope.user.id)
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a document within the authenticated scope.

  Returns `{:error, :not_found}` when the document does not exist or belongs to
  another user, so callers can treat inaccessible documents as missing.

  ## Examples

      iex> fetch_document(scope, "123")
      {:ok, %Document{}}

      iex> fetch_document(scope, "999")
      {:error, :not_found}

  """
  def fetch_document(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Document, id: id, user_id: scope.user.id) do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      document -> {:ok, document}
    end
  end

  def get_document_with_content!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    ec_query =
      from ec in ExtractedContent,
        order_by: [desc: ec.inserted_at, desc: ec.id],
        preload: :review_decision

    Document
    |> Repo.get_by!(id: id, user_id: scope.user.id)
    |> Repo.preload(extracted_content: ec_query)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a document.

  ## Examples

      iex> create_document(scope, %{field: value})
      {:ok, %Document{}}

      iex> create_document(scope, %{field: bad_value})
      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}}

  """
  def create_document(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    Ecto.Multi.new()
    |> Ecto.Multi.insert(:document, Document.changeset(%Document{}, attrs, scope))
    |> Oban.insert(:ocr_job, fn %{document: document} ->
      DocumentProcessing.ocr_job(document, scope.user.base_currency, nil)
    end)
    |> Repo.transaction()
    |> case do
      {:ok, %{document: document}} ->
        broadcast_document(scope, {:created, document})
        {:ok, document}

      {:error, :document, changeset, _changes} ->
        {:error, changeset}

      # Should not happen: the job insert runs in the same transaction and its
      # failure rolls back the document. Mapped to a changeset so upload callers
      # still clean up the stored object on any insert failure.
      {:error, :ocr_job, changeset, _changes} ->
        {:error, changeset}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a document.

  ## Examples

      iex> update_document(scope, document, %{field: new_value})
      {:ok, %Document{}}

      iex> update_document(scope, document, %{field: bad_value})
      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}}

  """
  def update_document(%Scope{} = scope, %Document{} = document, attrs) do
    true = document.user_id == scope.user.id

    with {:ok, document = %Document{}} <-
           document
           |> Document.changeset(attrs, scope)
           |> Repo.update() do
      broadcast_document(scope, {:updated, document})
      {:ok, document}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Deletes a document.

  ## Examples

      iex> delete_document(scope, document)
      {:ok, %Document{}}

      iex> delete_document(scope, document)
      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}}

  """
  def delete_document(%Scope{} = scope, %Document{} = document) do
    true = document.user_id == scope.user.id

    document
    |> Ecto.Changeset.change()
    |> Ecto.Changeset.foreign_key_constraint(:id,
      name: :journal_entries_review_decision_id_fkey,
      message: "has a posted journal entry and cannot be deleted"
    )
    |> Repo.delete()
    |> case do
      {:ok, document} ->
        _ = Storage.delete_object(document.object_key)
        broadcast_document(scope, {:deleted, document})
        {:ok, document}

      {:error, changeset} ->
        {:error, changeset}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Returns an `%Ecto.Changeset{}` for tracking document changes.

  ## Examples

      iex> change_document(scope, document)
      %Ecto.Changeset{data: %Document{}}

  """
  def change_document(%Scope{} = scope, %Document{} = document, attrs \\ %{}) do
    true = document.user_id == scope.user.id

    Document.changeset(document, attrs, scope)
  end
end

defmodule ZaimuTomo.FinancialAccounts do
  @moduledoc """
  Financial accounts and their dated balance snapshots.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias Ecto.Multi
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounts.Scope
  alias ZaimuTomo.FinancialAccounts.{BalanceSnapshot, FinancialAccount}
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo

  def subscribe_financial_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(ZaimuTomo.PubSub, topic(scope))
  end

  def list_financial_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    FinancialAccount
    |> where(user_id: ^scope.user.id)
    |> order_by([account], asc: account.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_financial_accounts_with_latest_balance(%Scope{} = scope) do
    latest_balances =
      scope
      |> latest_balance_snapshots()
      |> Map.new(&{&1.financial_account_id, &1})

    Enum.map(list_financial_accounts(scope), fn account ->
      %{account: account, balance_snapshot: Map.get(latest_balances, account.id)}
    end)
  end

  def list_net_worth_by_currency(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope
    |> list_financial_accounts_with_latest_balance()
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil(&1.balance_snapshot))
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.account.currency)
    |> Enum.map(fn {currency, accounts} ->
      %{
        currency: currency,
        total_cents: Enum.sum_by(accounts, & &1.balance_snapshot.amount_cents),
        account_count: length(accounts)
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.currency)
  end

  def list_savings_accounts_with_latest_balance(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope
    |> list_financial_accounts_with_latest_balance()
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.account.account_type == :savings))
  end

  def list_cash_accounts_with_latest_balance(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope
    |> list_financial_accounts_with_latest_balance()
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.account.account_type == :cash))
  end

  def list_investment_accounts_with_latest_balance(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope
    |> list_financial_accounts_with_latest_balance()
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.account.account_type == :investment))
  end

  def get_financial_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    Repo.get_by!(FinancialAccount, id: id, user_id: scope.user.id)
  end

  def create_financial_account_with_balance(%Scope{} = scope, account_attrs, balance_attrs) do
    multi =
      Multi.new()
      |> Multi.insert(
        :financial_account,
        FinancialAccount.changeset(%FinancialAccount{}, account_attrs, scope)
      )
      |> Multi.insert(:balance_snapshot, fn %{financial_account: account} ->
        BalanceSnapshot.changeset(
          %BalanceSnapshot{},
          Map.put(balance_attrs, :financial_account_id, account.id)
        )
      end)

    case Repo.transaction(multi) do
      {:ok, %{financial_account: account, balance_snapshot: snapshot}} ->
        broadcast(scope, {:created, account})
        {:ok, %{account: account, balance_snapshot: snapshot}}

      {:error, _operation, changeset, _changes} ->
        {:error, changeset}
    end
  end

  def update_financial_account(%Scope{} = scope, %FinancialAccount{} = account, attrs) do
    true = account.user_id == scope.user.id

    case account |> FinancialAccount.changeset(attrs, scope) |> Repo.update() do
      {:ok, updated_account} ->
        broadcast(scope, {:updated, updated_account})
        {:ok, updated_account}

      {:error, changeset} ->
        {:error, changeset}
    end
  end

  def delete_financial_account(%Scope{} = scope, %FinancialAccount{} = account) do
    true = account.user_id == scope.user.id

    case Repo.delete(account) do
      {:ok, deleted_account} ->
        broadcast(scope, {:deleted, deleted_account})
        {:ok, deleted_account}

      {:error, changeset} ->
        {:error, changeset}
    end
  end

  def change_financial_account(%Scope{} = scope, %FinancialAccount{} = account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    true = account.user_id == scope.user.id
    FinancialAccount.changeset(account, attrs, scope)
  end

  def list_balance_snapshots(%Scope{} = scope, %FinancialAccount{} = account) do
    true = account.user_id == scope.user.id

    BalanceSnapshot
    |> where(financial_account_id: ^account.id)
    |> order_by([snapshot],
      desc: snapshot.recorded_on,
      desc: snapshot.inserted_at,
      desc: snapshot.id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc "Returns the current user's balance snapshots in the inclusive date range."
  def list_balance_history(%Scope{} = scope, %Date{} = start_date, %Date{} = end_date) do
    scope
    |> scoped_balance_snapshots()
    |> where(
      [snapshot, _account],
      snapshot.recorded_on >= ^start_date and snapshot.recorded_on <= ^end_date
    )
    |> order_by([snapshot, _account],
      asc: snapshot.financial_account_id,
      asc: snapshot.recorded_on,
      asc: snapshot.inserted_at,
      asc: snapshot.id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc "Returns each user's account's latest snapshot before the history window."
  def list_balance_history_baseline(%Scope{} = scope, %Date{} = before_date) do
    scope
    |> scoped_balance_snapshots()
    |> where([snapshot, _account], snapshot.recorded_on < ^before_date)
    |> latest_balance_query()
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def record_balance(%Scope{} = scope, %FinancialAccount{} = account, attrs) do
    true = account.user_id == scope.user.id

    result =
      attrs
      |> Map.put(:financial_account_id, account.id)
      |> then(&BalanceSnapshot.changeset(%BalanceSnapshot{}, &1))
      |> Repo.insert()

    case result do
      {:ok, snapshot} ->
        broadcast(scope, {:balance_recorded, snapshot})
        {:ok, snapshot}

      {:error, changeset} ->
        {:error, changeset}
    end
  end

  def change_balance_snapshot(%BalanceSnapshot{} = snapshot, attrs \\ %{}) do
    BalanceSnapshot.changeset(snapshot, attrs)
  end

  defp latest_balance_snapshots(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope
    |> scoped_balance_snapshots()
    |> latest_balance_query()
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp latest_balance_query(query) do
    query
    |> distinct([snapshot, _account], snapshot.financial_account_id)
    |> order_by([snapshot, _account],
      asc: snapshot.financial_account_id,
      desc: snapshot.recorded_on,
      desc: snapshot.inserted_at,
      desc: snapshot.id
    )
  end

  defp scoped_balance_snapshots(%Scope{} = scope) do
    from(snapshot in BalanceSnapshot,
      join: account in FinancialAccount,
      on: account.id == snapshot.financial_account_id,
      where: account.user_id == ^scope.user.id
    )
  end

  defp topic(scope), do: "user:#{scope.user.id}:financial_accounts"

  defp broadcast(scope, message),
    do: Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(ZaimuTomo.PubSub, topic(scope), message)
end

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Documents.FingerprintBackfill do
  @moduledoc """
  Idempotent, online backfill of exact-byte fingerprints for rows created
  before fingerprints existed.

  1. Every document with a null `content_sha256` is read through
     `ZaimuTomo.Storage` and hashed. A missing or unreadable object is
     reported and left null; no other value is ever stored in its place.
  2. Every journal entry with a null `source_document_sha256` receives its
     source document's fingerprint, one entry per update and oldest first, so
     the first posting of a file keeps it. A unique-index violation (a same-user
     historical duplicate) affects only that row: it is reported with the entry
     it collides with and left null. Ledger rows are never deleted or merged.

  A human may resolve a reported collision by listing the later entry in
  `:confirm_reuse`; the backfill then sets its digest and
  `source_file_reuse_confirmed` in one update. This is the only permitted
  update of an existing entry's fingerprint (spec D7), so it must run before
  any database-level immutability trigger on `journal_entries` exists, or that
  trigger must allow it.

  The report contains row IDs and counts only, never bytes or digests. The
  partial unique index already exists, so concurrent postings cannot create a
  same-user duplicate while this runs.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.JournalEntry
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Document
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.Fingerprint
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review.ReviewDecision
  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage

  @type collision :: %{journal_entry_id: integer(), user_id: integer(), conflicts_with: integer()}

  @type summary :: %{
          documents_hashed: non_neg_integer(),
          documents_already_complete: non_neg_integer(),
          missing_objects: [integer()],
          read_failures: [%{document_id: integer(), reason: term()}],
          entries_updated: non_neg_integer(),
          entries_already_complete: non_neg_integer(),
          entries_reuse_confirmed: [integer()],
          entries_source_unavailable: [integer()],
          collisions: [collision()],
          unused_reuse_confirmations: [integer()]
        }

  @doc """
  Runs the backfill.

  Returns `{:ok, summary}` when historical coverage is complete, and
  `{:error, summary}` when any object is missing or unreadable, an entry's
  source fingerprint is unavailable, or a collision awaits human review.

  Options:

    * `:confirm_reuse` — journal entry IDs a human confirmed as legitimate
      reuses of an already posted file. Applied only to an entry whose plain
      update collides; otherwise reported as unused.
  """
  @spec run(keyword()) :: {:ok, summary()} | {:error, summary()}
  def run(opts \\ []) do
    confirm_reuse = opts |> Keyword.get(:confirm_reuse, []) |> MapSet.new()

    summary =
      empty_summary()
      |> backfill_documents()
      |> backfill_journal_entries(confirm_reuse)
      |> finalize(confirm_reuse)

    if complete?(summary), do: {:ok, summary}, else: {:error, summary}
  end

  @spec format_summary(summary()) :: String.t()
  def format_summary(summary) do
    [
      "Fingerprint backfill summary: " <>
        "documents_hashed=#{summary.documents_hashed} " <>
        "documents_already_complete=#{summary.documents_already_complete} " <>
        "missing_objects=#{length(summary.missing_objects)} " <>
        "read_failures=#{length(summary.read_failures)} " <>
        "entries_updated=#{summary.entries_updated} " <>
        "entries_already_complete=#{summary.entries_already_complete} " <>
        "entries_reuse_confirmed=#{length(summary.entries_reuse_confirmed)} " <>
        "entries_source_unavailable=#{length(summary.entries_source_unavailable)} " <>
        "collisions=#{length(summary.collisions)}"
      | Enum.map(summary.missing_objects, &"Missing object for document #{&1}") ++
          Enum.map(summary.read_failures, &format_read_failure/1) ++
          Enum.map(summary.entries_source_unavailable, &format_source_unavailable/1) ++
          Enum.map(summary.collisions, &format_collision/1) ++
          Enum.map(summary.entries_reuse_confirmed, &"Confirmed reuse for journal entry #{&1}") ++
          Enum.map(summary.unused_reuse_confirmations, &format_unused_confirmation/1) ++
          coverage_line(summary)
    ]
    |> Enum.join("\n")
  end

  # -- Documents ---------------------------------------------------------------

  defp backfill_documents(summary) do
    already_complete =
      Repo.aggregate(from(d in Document, where: not is_nil(d.content_sha256)), :count)

    from(d in Document,
      where: is_nil(d.content_sha256),
      order_by: [asc: d.id],
      select: {d.id, d.object_key}
    )
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.reduce(%{summary | documents_already_complete: already_complete}, &hash_document/2)
  end

  defp hash_document({document_id, object_key}, summary) do
    case Storage.read_object(object_key) do
      {:ok, body} ->
        # Conditional on the same key and a still-null digest, so a concurrent
        # file replacement (which records its own digest) is never overwritten.
        {count, _} =
          from(d in Document,
            where:
              d.id == ^document_id and d.object_key == ^object_key and
                is_nil(d.content_sha256)
          )
          |> Repo.update_all(set: [content_sha256: Fingerprint.sha256(body)])

        if count == 1,
          do: %{summary | documents_hashed: summary.documents_hashed + 1},
          else: %{summary | documents_already_complete: summary.documents_already_complete + 1}

      {:error, :not_found} ->
        %{summary | missing_objects: [document_id | summary.missing_objects]}

      {:error, reason} ->
        failure = %{document_id: document_id, reason: reason}
        %{summary | read_failures: [failure | summary.read_failures]}
    end
  end

  # -- Journal entries ---------------------------------------------------------

  defp backfill_journal_entries(summary, confirm_reuse) do
    already_complete =
      Repo.aggregate(
        from(je in JournalEntry, where: not is_nil(je.source_document_sha256)),
        :count
      )

    from(je in JournalEntry,
      left_join: rd in ReviewDecision,
      on: rd.id == je.review_decision_id,
      left_join: ec in ExtractedContent,
      on: ec.id == rd.extracted_content_id and ec.user_id == je.user_id,
      left_join: d in Document,
      on: d.id == ec.document_id and d.user_id == je.user_id,
      where: is_nil(je.source_document_sha256),
      order_by: [asc: je.inserted_at, asc: je.id],
      select: {je, d.content_sha256}
    )
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.reduce(
      %{summary | entries_already_complete: already_complete},
      &backfill_entry(&1, &2, confirm_reuse)
    )
  end

  defp backfill_entry({entry, nil}, summary, _confirm_reuse) do
    %{summary | entries_source_unavailable: [entry.id | summary.entries_source_unavailable]}
  end

  defp backfill_entry({entry, digest}, summary, confirm_reuse) do
    case update_entry(entry, %{source_document_sha256: digest}) do
      {:ok, _entry} ->
        %{summary | entries_updated: summary.entries_updated + 1}

      {:error, :collision} ->
        if MapSet.member?(confirm_reuse, entry.id) do
          confirm_reuse(entry, digest, summary)
        else
          collision = %{
            journal_entry_id: entry.id,
            user_id: entry.user_id,
            conflicts_with: conflicting_entry_id(entry.user_id, digest)
          }

          %{summary | collisions: [collision | summary.collisions]}
        end
    end
  end

  defp confirm_reuse(entry, digest, summary) do
    attrs = %{source_document_sha256: digest, source_file_reuse_confirmed: true}

    # A confirmed reuse is outside the partial index, so it cannot collide.
    {:ok, _entry} = update_entry(entry, attrs)
    %{summary | entries_reuse_confirmed: [entry.id | summary.entries_reuse_confirmed]}
  end

  # The fingerprint is derived metadata, not an edit: keep `updated_at`, which
  # orders the user's journal list.
  defp update_entry(entry, attrs) do
    entry
    |> JournalEntry.changeset_for_fingerprint_backfill(attrs)
    |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:updated_at, entry.updated_at)
    |> Repo.update()
    |> case do
      {:ok, entry} ->
        {:ok, entry}

      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} ->
        if source_file_collision?(changeset),
          do: {:error, :collision},
          else: raise(Ecto.InvalidChangesetError, action: :update, changeset: changeset)
    end
  end

  defp source_file_collision?(%Ecto.Changeset{errors: errors}) do
    Enum.any?(errors, fn {_field, {_message, opts}} ->
      opts[:constraint] == :unique and
        opts[:constraint_name] == JournalEntry.duplicate_source_file_index()
    end)
  end

  defp conflicting_entry_id(user_id, digest) do
    from(je in JournalEntry,
      where: je.user_id == ^user_id and je.source_document_sha256 == ^digest,
      where: not je.source_file_reuse_confirmed,
      select: je.id,
      limit: 1
    )
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  # -- Summary -----------------------------------------------------------------

  defp empty_summary do
    %{
      documents_hashed: 0,
      documents_already_complete: 0,
      missing_objects: [],
      read_failures: [],
      entries_updated: 0,
      entries_already_complete: 0,
      entries_reuse_confirmed: [],
      entries_source_unavailable: [],
      collisions: [],
      unused_reuse_confirmations: []
    }
  end

  defp finalize(summary, confirm_reuse) do
    applied = MapSet.new(summary.entries_reuse_confirmed)

    %{
      summary
      | missing_objects: Enum.reverse(summary.missing_objects),
        read_failures: Enum.reverse(summary.read_failures),
        entries_reuse_confirmed: Enum.reverse(summary.entries_reuse_confirmed),
        entries_source_unavailable: Enum.reverse(summary.entries_source_unavailable),
        collisions: Enum.reverse(summary.collisions),
        unused_reuse_confirmations: confirm_reuse |> MapSet.difference(applied) |> Enum.sort()
    }
  end

  defp complete?(summary) do
    summary.missing_objects == [] and summary.read_failures == [] and
      summary.entries_source_unavailable == [] and summary.collisions == []
  end

  defp coverage_line(summary) do
    if complete?(summary),
      do: ["Historical fingerprint coverage is complete."],
      else: ["Historical fingerprint coverage is INCOMPLETE; see the rows above."]
  end

  defp format_read_failure(%{document_id: id, reason: reason}),
    do: "Read failure for document #{id}: #{inspect(reason)}"

  defp format_source_unavailable(id),
    do: "Journal entry #{id}: source document fingerprint unavailable"

  defp format_collision(%{journal_entry_id: id, user_id: user_id, conflicts_with: other}),
    do:
      "Collision: journal entry #{id} (user #{user_id}) has the same source file as " <>
        "entry #{other}; left null for human ledger review"

  defp format_unused_confirmation(id),
    do: "Reuse confirmation for journal entry #{id} not applied (no collision to resolve)"
end

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Accounting.LegacyBookingBackfill do
  @moduledoc """
  One-off backfill for journal entries that predate booking at posting time and
  are still missing a category or a need/want choice.

  An entry is completed only when the same user's posted entries from the same
  issuer (compared like the duplicate index, trimmed and case-insensitive) agree
  on every missing value. Values the entry already has are kept. Anything else
  is reported for a person to book, so nothing is guessed from a similar name.

  Bookings a person already decided are passed at run time as `:manual`, so no
  real ledger data lives in the repository. They are keyed by entry ID and
  normalized issuer so they cannot land on another row, and go through
  `Accounting.post_entry/6`, exactly like the invoice page's Book form.

  It is a dry run unless called with `confirm: true`. Each entry is updated in
  its own transaction together with a `journal_entry_posted` event marked with
  `source: "legacy_booking_backfill"` that records the prior state. For those copied bookings, tax claims and notes
  are left alone, and `updated_at` is kept so old entries do not jump to the top
  of the journal.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias Ecto.Multi
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.JournalEntry
  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.TaxDeductionClaim
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing.ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent
  alias ZaimuTomo.Repo
  alias ZaimuTomo.Review.ReviewDecision

  @source "legacy_booking_backfill"

  @type match :: %{
          required(:entry) => JournalEntry.t(),
          required(:document_id) => integer(),
          required(:category) => String.t(),
          required(:need_or_want) => String.t(),
          required(:source) => :precedent | :manual,
          optional(:precedent_count) => pos_integer(),
          optional(:tax_status) => String.t() | nil
        }

  @type unmatched :: %{
          entry: JournalEntry.t(),
          document_id: integer(),
          reason: :no_history | :conflicting_history
        }

  @type summary :: %{
          confirmed: boolean(),
          matched: [match()],
          applied: [match()],
          unmatched: [unmatched()],
          failed: [%{match: match(), errors: term()}]
        }

  @doc """
  Plans the backfill and, with `confirm: true`, applies it.

  Returns `{:error, summary}` only when an update failed. Unmatched entries are
  expected and left for manual booking.

  Options:

    * `:confirm` - apply the plan instead of only reporting it.
    * `:manual` - decided bookings as a map of `{entry_id, normalized_issuer}`
      to `%{category: _, need_or_want: _, tax_status: _}`. Defaults to none.
  """
  @spec run(keyword()) :: {:ok, summary()} | {:error, summary()}
  def run(opts \\ []) do
    confirmed = Keyword.get(opts, :confirm, false)
    %{matched: matched, unmatched: unmatched} = plan(Keyword.get(opts, :manual, %{}))
    %{applied: applied, failed: failed} = apply_matches(matched, confirmed)

    summary = %{
      confirmed: confirmed,
      matched: matched,
      applied: applied,
      unmatched: unmatched,
      failed: failed
    }

    {if(failed == [], do: :ok, else: :error), summary}
  end

  @spec format_summary(summary()) :: String.t()
  def format_summary(summary) do
    verb = if summary.confirmed, do: "Booked", else: "Would book"
    mode = if summary.confirmed, do: "applied", else: "dry run"

    [
      "Legacy booking backfill (#{mode}): matched=#{length(summary.matched)} " <>
        "applied=#{length(summary.applied)} unmatched=#{length(summary.unmatched)} " <>
        "failed=#{length(summary.failed)}",
      Enum.map(summary.matched, &format_match(&1, verb)),
      Enum.map(summary.unmatched, &format_unmatched/1),
      Enum.map(summary.failed, &format_failure/1),
      if(summary.confirmed, do: [], else: "Nothing changed. Re-run with confirm: true to apply.")
    ]
    |> List.flatten()
    |> Enum.join("\n")
  end

  defp plan(manual) do
    precedents = precedents()

    targets()
    |> Enum.map(&classify(&1, precedents, manual))
    |> Enum.group_by(&elem(&1, 0), &elem(&1, 1))
    |> then(&%{matched: Map.get(&1, :matched, []), unmatched: Map.get(&1, :unmatched, [])})
  end

  defp targets do
    Repo.all(
      from e in JournalEntry,
        join: d in ReviewDecision,
        on: d.id == e.review_decision_id,
        join: c in ExtractedContent,
        on: c.id == d.extracted_content_id,
        left_join: t in TaxDeductionClaim,
        on: t.journal_entry_id == e.id,
        where: is_nil(e.category) or is_nil(e.need_or_want),
        order_by: e.id,
        select: %{
          entry: e,
          document_id: c.document_id,
          tax_status: t.status,
          issuer_key: fragment("lower(btrim(?))", e.issuer)
        }
    )
  end

  defp precedents do
    from(e in JournalEntry,
      where: e.status == "posted",
      where: not is_nil(e.category) and not is_nil(e.need_or_want),
      where: fragment("btrim(?) <> ''", e.issuer),
      group_by: [e.user_id, fragment("lower(btrim(?))", e.issuer), e.category, e.need_or_want],
      select: %{
        user_id: e.user_id,
        issuer_key: fragment("lower(btrim(?))", e.issuer),
        category: e.category,
        need_or_want: e.need_or_want,
        count: count(e.id)
      }
    )
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.group_by(&{&1.user_id, &1.issuer_key})
  end

  defp classify(%{entry: entry, issuer_key: issuer_key} = target, precedents, manual) do
    row = Map.take(target, [:entry, :document_id, :tax_status])

    case Map.fetch(manual, {entry.id, issuer_key}) do
      {:ok, decision} -> {:matched, row |> Map.merge(decision) |> Map.put(:source, :manual)}
      :error -> classify_from_history(row, Map.get(precedents, {entry.user_id, issuer_key}, []))
    end
  end

  defp classify_from_history(%{entry: entry} = row, history) do
    case history |> Enum.map(&completed_booking(entry, &1)) |> Enum.uniq() do
      [] ->
        {:unmatched, Map.put(row, :reason, :no_history)}

      [{category, need_or_want}] ->
        precedent_count = history |> Enum.map(& &1.count) |> Enum.sum()

        {:matched,
         Map.merge(row, %{
           category: category,
           need_or_want: need_or_want,
           precedent_count: precedent_count,
           source: :precedent
         })}

      _conflicting ->
        {:unmatched, Map.put(row, :reason, :conflicting_history)}
    end
  end

  # Precedents only need to agree on what the entry is missing.
  defp completed_booking(entry, precedent) do
    {entry.category || precedent.category, entry.need_or_want || precedent.need_or_want}
  end

  defp apply_matches(_matched, false), do: %{applied: [], failed: []}

  defp apply_matches(matched, true) do
    results = Enum.map(matched, &{&1, apply_match(&1)})

    %{
      applied: for({match, {:ok, _}} <- results, do: match),
      failed:
        for({match, {:error, changeset}} <- results) do
          %{match: match, errors: changeset.errors}
        end
    }
  end

  defp apply_match(%{source: :manual, entry: entry} = match) do
    Accounting.post_entry(
      entry,
      entry.user_id,
      match.category,
      match.need_or_want,
      entry.notes,
      %{"status" => match.tax_status}
    )
  end

  defp apply_match(%{source: :precedent} = match) do
    Multi.new()
    |> Multi.update(:entry, booking_changeset(match))
    |> Multi.insert(:event, &event_changeset(&1.entry, match))
    |> Repo.transaction()
    |> case do
      {:ok, changes} -> {:ok, changes}
      {:error, _step, changeset, _changes} -> {:error, changeset}
    end
  end

  defp booking_changeset(%{entry: entry} = match) do
    entry
    |> JournalEntry.changeset_for_categorize(%{
      category: match.category,
      need_or_want: match.need_or_want,
      status: "posted"
    })
    |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:updated_at, entry.updated_at)
  end

  defp event_changeset(booked_entry, %{entry: previous} = match) do
    Accounting.posted_event_changeset(booked_entry, match.tax_status, %{
      source: @source,
      precedent_count: match.precedent_count,
      previous_status: previous.status,
      previous_category: previous.category,
      previous_need_or_want: previous.need_or_want
    })
  end

  defp format_match(%{entry: entry} = match, verb) do
    "#{verb} entry #{entry.id} (#{entry.issuer}) as #{match.category} / #{match.need_or_want} " <>
      match_origin(match) <> "."
  end

  defp match_origin(%{source: :manual, tax_status: tax_status}),
    do: "from a manual decision, tax status #{tax_status}"

  defp match_origin(%{source: :precedent, precedent_count: count}),
    do: "from #{count} earlier posting(s)"

  defp format_unmatched(%{entry: entry, document_id: document_id, reason: reason}) do
    "Book by hand: entry #{entry.id} (#{entry.issuer}) at /documents/#{document_id}: " <>
      unmatched_reason(reason) <> "."
  end

  defp unmatched_reason(:no_history), do: "no earlier posting from this issuer"
  defp unmatched_reason(:conflicting_history), do: "earlier postings disagree"

  defp format_failure(%{match: %{entry: entry}, errors: errors}) do
    "Failed entry #{entry.id}: #{inspect(errors)}"
  end
end

11	  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and

31	    %__MODULE__{user: user}

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounts.User

  defstruct user: nil

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{}

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Release do
  @moduledoc """
  Release helpers used by deployment tasks.
  """

  @app :zaimu_tomo

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.LegacyBookingBackfill
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.FingerprintBackfill
  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage.{Migration, Verification}

  def migrate do
    load_app()

    for repo <- repos() do
      {:ok, _, _} = Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(repo, &Ecto.Migrator.run(&1, :up, all: true))
    end
  end

  def rollback(repo, version) do
    load_app()
    {:ok, _, _} = Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(repo, &Ecto.Migrator.run(&1, :down, to: version))
  end

  def migrate_to_s3!(source_dir) when is_binary(source_dir) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(Migration.migrate(source_dir), Migration)
  end

  def migrate_to_s3_from_env! do
    System.fetch_env!("SOURCE_DIR")
    |> migrate_to_s3!()
  end

  def backfill_document_fingerprints!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(FingerprintBackfill.run(opts), FingerprintBackfill)
  end

  def backfill_legacy_bookings!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(LegacyBookingBackfill.run(opts), LegacyBookingBackfill)
  end

  def verify_storage! do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(Verification.verify(), Verification)
  end

  def recover_stuck_documents!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    groups = DocumentProcessing.Recovery.list_stuck()
    Enum.each(groups, &print_stuck_group/1)

    dispatch_recovery(Keyword.get(opts, :confirm, false), groups)
  end

  defp dispatch_recovery(true, groups) do
    jobs = DocumentProcessing.Recovery.enqueue_stuck(groups)
    IO.puts("Enqueued #{length(jobs)} OCR jobs.")
    groups
  end

  defp dispatch_recovery(false, groups) do
    count = groups |> Enum.map(&length(&1.document_ids)) |> Enum.sum()
    IO.puts("Dry run: #{count} stuck documents — nothing enqueued.")
    IO.puts("Re-run with confirm: true (or CONFIRM=true) to enqueue.")
    groups
  end

  defp print_stuck_group(%{user_id: user_id, currency: currency, document_ids: document_ids}) do
    IO.puts("user #{user_id} (#{currency}): document ids #{Enum.join(document_ids, ", ")}")
  end

  defp repos do
    Application.fetch_env!(@app, :ecto_repos)
  end

  defp load_app do
    Application.load(@app)
  end

  defp start_app do
    load_app()

    # Eval nodes run maintenance only: no queues, no plugins, no leadership, so
    # a short-lived node never grabs a job and dies mid-run (leaving it orphaned
    # until Lifeline rescues it).
    oban = Application.fetch_env!(@app, Oban)

    Application.put_env(
      @app,
      Oban,
      Keyword.merge(oban, queues: false, plugins: false, peer: false)
    )

    case Application.ensure_all_started(@app) do
      {:ok, _started} -> :ok
      {:error, reason} -> raise "could not start #{@app}: #{inspect(reason)}"
    end
  end

  defp report_or_raise({status, summary}, formatter) do
    IO.puts(formatter.format_summary(summary))

    case status do
      :ok -> summary
      :error -> raise "maintenance command failed"
    end
  end
end

defmodule ZaimuTomo.DataCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the setup for tests requiring
  access to the application's data layer.

  You may define functions here to be used as helpers in
  your tests.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use ZaimuTomo.DataCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  alias Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox

  using do
    quote do
      alias ZaimuTomo.Repo

      import Ecto
      import Ecto.Changeset
      import Ecto.Query
      import ZaimuTomo.DataCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    ZaimuTomo.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    :ok
  end

  @doc """
  Sets up the sandbox based on the test tags.
  """
  def setup_sandbox(tags) do
    pid = Sandbox.start_owner!(ZaimuTomo.Repo, shared: not tags[:async])
    on_exit(fn -> Sandbox.stop_owner(pid) end)
  end

  @doc """
  Makes every insert into `table` fail at the database with the constraint
  error that `changeset` declares for `field`.

  A test-owned `BEFORE INSERT` trigger raises the matching SQLSTATE with the
  declared constraint name, so Ecto maps it to a real
  `{:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}}` without altering the table's own constraints.
  The name comes from the changeset (not a hard-coded string), so a dependency
  renaming or dropping the constraint fails here instead of silently. The
  trigger and its `pg_temp` function roll back with the sandbox transaction.

      fail_inserts!("oban_jobs", Oban.Job.new(%{}, worker: "X"), :max_attempts)
  """
  def fail_inserts!(table, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset, field) do
    %{constraint: name, type: type} =
      Enum.find(changeset.constraints, &(&1.field == field)) ||
        raise ArgumentError,
              "#{inspect(changeset.data.__struct__)} declares no constraint on #{field}"

    sqlstate = %{check: "check_violation", foreign_key: "foreign_key_violation"}[type]

    ZaimuTomo.Repo.query!("""
    CREATE FUNCTION pg_temp.fail_#{table}_insert() RETURNS trigger AS $$
    BEGIN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'test-injected failure' USING ERRCODE = '#{sqlstate}', CONSTRAINT = '#{name}';
    END
    $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql
    """)

    ZaimuTomo.Repo.query!(
      "CREATE TRIGGER fail_#{table}_insert BEFORE INSERT ON #{table} " <>
        "FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION pg_temp.fail_#{table}_insert()"
    )

    :ok
  end

  @doc """
  A helper that transforms changeset errors into a map of messages.

      assert {:error, changeset} = Accounts.create_user(%{password: "REDACTED"})
      assert "password is too REDACTED" in errors_on(changeset).password
      assert %{password: ["password is too REDACTED"]} = errors_on(changeset)

  """
  def errors_on(changeset) do
    Ecto.Changeset.traverse_errors(changeset, fn {message, opts} ->
      Regex.replace(~r"%{(\w+)}", message, fn _, key ->
        opts |> Keyword.get(String.to_existing_atom(key), key) |> to_string()
      end)
    end)
  end
end

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Review.EventLog do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounts.User

  schema "event_logs" do
    field :event_type, :string
    field :invoice_id, :string
    field :metadata, :map
    field :status, :string

    belongs_to :user, User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  def changeset_for_create(attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{}
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :event_type,
      :invoice_id,
      :user_id,
      :metadata,
      :status
    ])
    |> validate_required([:event_type, :metadata])
    |> validate_inclusion(:status, ["pending", "completed", "failed"])
    |> foreign_key_constraint(:user_id)
  end
end

1	# Kamal 2 deployment for ZaimuTomo on a Hetzner VPS reached through WireGuard.
2	# SSH reaches the VPS on its public IP. The app itself is exposed only on WireGuard.
3	# Keep real host/IP values in environment variables or .kamal/secrets, not in git.
4	
5	service: zaimu-tomo
6	image: acramatte/zaimu-tomo
7	
8	ssh:
9	  user: <%= ENV.fetch("KAMAL_SSH_USER", "kamal") %>
10	
11	# This VPS runs Watchtower. Kamal should remain in control of deployments, so
12	# exclude the app container from automatic Watchtower updates.
13	labels:
14	  com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable: "false"
15	
16	servers:
17	  web:
18	    hosts:
19	      # SSH target. Kamal connects here, while the proxy below binds to the VPN IP only.
20	      - <%= ENV.fetch("KAMAL_SSH_HOST") %>
21	    # If another reverse proxy already owns ports 80/443 on this VPS, uncomment this
22	    # and route that proxy to the app container/port yourself instead of using Kamal Proxy.

28	  app_port: 4000

# Kamal 2 deployment for ZaimuTomo on a Hetzner VPS reached through WireGuard.
# SSH reaches the VPS on its public IP. The app itself is exposed only on WireGuard.
# Keep real host/IP values in environment variables or .kamal/secrets, not in git.

service: zaimu-tomo
image: acramatte/zaimu-tomo

ssh:
  user: <%= ENV.fetch("KAMAL_SSH_USER", "kamal") %>

# This VPS runs Watchtower. Kamal should remain in control of deployments, so
# exclude the app container from automatic Watchtower updates.
labels:
  com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable: "false"

servers:
  web:
    hosts:
      # SSH target. Kamal connects here, while the proxy below binds to the VPN IP only.
      - <%= ENV.fetch("KAMAL_SSH_HOST") %>
    # If another reverse proxy already owns ports 80/443 on this VPS, uncomment this
    # and route that proxy to the app container/port yourself instead of using Kamal Proxy.
    # proxy: false

proxy:
  ssl: false
  host: <%= ENV.fetch("PHX_HOST", "10.0.0.1") %>
  app_port: 4000
  forward_headers: true
  healthcheck:
    path: /health
    interval: 3
    timeout: 3
  run:
    # Keep Kamal Proxy reachable only from the VPN interface.
    # If your current reverse proxy binds 0.0.0.0:80/443, either move it to the
    # public interface only, change these ports, or set `proxy: false` above.
    bind_ips:
      - <%= ENV.fetch("KAMAL_PROXY_BIND_IP", "10.0.0.1") %>
    # nginx already owns 0.0.0.0:80 on the VPS. Kamal Proxy listens on an
    # unreserved VPN-only port, and nginx forwards http://10.0.0.1 to it.
    http_port: 8083
    https_port: 8443

registry:
  server: ghcr.io
  username: acramatte
  password:
    - KAMAL_REGISTRY_PASSWORD

builder:
  arch: amd64

env:
  clear:
    PHX_SERVER: "true"
    PHX_HOST: <%= ENV.fetch("PHX_HOST", "10.0.0.1") %>
    PORT: "4000"
    POOL_SIZE: "10"
    AI_EXTRACTOR_BACKEND: "nousresearch"
    AI_EXTRACTOR_MODEL: "ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b"
    AI_VERIFIER_BACKEND: "nousresearch"
    AI_VERIFIER_MODEL: "qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b"
    MISTRAL_URL: "https://api.mistral.ai/v1"
    S3_ENDPOINT: "http://zaimu-tomo-rustfs:9000"
    S3_REGION: "eu-central-1"
    S3_BUCKET: "zaimu-tomo-prod"
    S3_PATH_STYLE: "true"
    S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: "zaimu_tomo"
    LANGFUSE_HOST: <%= ENV.fetch("LANGFUSE_HOST", "https://cloud.langfuse.com") %>
    TYPESAFE_URL: <%= ENV.fetch("TYPESAFE_URL", "https://api.typesafe.ai") %>
    TYPESAFE_MODEL: <%= ENV.fetch("TYPESAFE_MODEL", "jev-latest") %>
    TYPESAFE_REVIEW_THRESHOLD: <%= ENV.fetch("TYPESAFE_REVIEW_THRESHOLD", "0.7") %>
    TYPESAFE_RECEIVE_TIMEOUT: <%= ENV.fetch("TYPESAFE_RECEIVE_TIMEOUT", "30000") %>
    TYPESAFE_TOTAL_TIMEOUT: <%= ENV.fetch("TYPESAFE_TOTAL_TIMEOUT", "10000") %>
    TYPESAFE_MAX_RETRIES: <%= ENV.fetch("TYPESAFE_MAX_RETRIES", "0") %>
    TYPESAFE_MAX_CONCURRENCY: <%= ENV.fetch("TYPESAFE_MAX_CONCURRENCY", "2") %>
    OTEL_SERVICE_NAME: "zaimu-tomo"
  secret:
    - SECRET_KEY_BASE
    - DATABASE_URL
    - MISTRAL_API_KEY
    - S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    - NOUSRESEARCH_API_KEY
    - TYPESAFE_API_KEY
    - LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY
    - LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY

# Retain legacy local uploads through the migration release. Phase 5 removes
# this version-dependent path only after the RustFS copy, verification, and
# restore check succeed.
volumes:
  - zaimu_tomo_uploads:/app/lib/zaimu_tomo-0.1.0/priv/uploads

accessories:
  # The app speaks S3 through the generic S3_* variables above. RustFS-specific
  # settings remain inside this self-hosted accessory.
  rustfs:
    # 1.0.0-beta.12
    image: rustfs/rustfs:1.0.0-beta.12@sha256:41fe89380f4120a337790c02af192c3fe7bb55c3edc2e6e9357b487b47c6ab21
    host: <%= ENV.fetch("KAMAL_SSH_HOST") %>
    labels:
      com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable: "false"
    env:
      clear:
        RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: "zaimu_tomo"
        RUSTFS_REGION: "eu-central-1"
        RUSTFS_ADDRESS: ":9000"
        RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ADDRESS: ":9001"
        RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE: "true"
        RUSTFS_OBS_LOG_DIRECTORY: "/logs"
      secret:
        - RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY
    directories:
      - data:/data
      - logs:/logs

  db:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    host: <%= ENV.fetch("KAMAL_SSH_HOST") %>
    labels:
      com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable: "false"
    port: "127.0.0.1:5433:5432"
    env:
      clear:
        POSTGRES_USER: zaimu_tomo
        POSTGRES_DB: zaimu_tomo_prod
        PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data
      secret:
        - POSTGRES_PASSWORD
    directories:
      - data:/var/lib/postgresql

aliases:
  console: app exec --interactive --reuse "bin/zaimu_tomo remote"
  migrate: app exec "bin/migrate"
  migrate_to_s3: app exec "bin/migrate_to_s3 /app/lib/zaimu_tomo-0.1.0/priv/uploads"
  verify_storage: app exec "bin/verify_storage"
  recover_stuck_documents: app exec "bin/recover_stuck_documents"
  backfill_document_fingerprints: app exec "bin/backfill_document_fingerprints"
  db_rollback: app exec "bin/zaimu_tomo eval 'ZaimuTomo.Release.rollback(ZaimuTomo.Repo, 1)'"
